links.comparator_used: Baseline prompt with no reading-level instruction (phase 1) versus sixth-grade request, rule-based prompting and direct readability targeting
links.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT responses to spine surgery questions (SMOG, Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, Coleman-Liau)
links.effect: Phase 2 (sixth-grade level request) yielded the most readable responses, with 51.11% meeting the sixth-grade level; simplified prompting was more effective than complex rule-based prompts; ChatGPT 4o was more readable than ChatGPT 5 in all phases except phase 1 (P < 0.001)
links.quote: Phase 2 yielded the most readable responses, with 51.11% meeting the sixth-grade level.

links.comparator_used: Baseline single response without follow-up clarification (phase 1)
links.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT responses after a follow-up clarification question (phase 1.5)
links.effect: Follow-up clarification questions were more effective than complex rule-based prompts; the abstract gives no phase 1.5 versus baseline numbers
links.quote: Follow-up clarification questions and simplified prompt engineering were more effective than complex rule-based prompts.

design_hint: reading-level prompt constraints and follow-up questioning
